title: Cleaning text and numbers

cells.text: New dataset: sign-ups for campus clubs. People typed them in by hand, so the data is **messy**: extra spaces, different capital letters, and fees saved as text like "$10". Cleaning data like this is a big part of every analyst's job.

cells.prompt: Press Run to load all 8 sign-ups. Look closely at the club column.
cells.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("club_signups.csv")
df

cells.text: `nunique()` counts the different values. It's a quick way to spot messy text, because "Chess" and "chess" count as 2 different clubs.

cells.prompt: There are really only 3 clubs: Chess, Robotics and Debate. How many different clubs will pandas count BEFORE cleaning? Pick one, then press Run.

cells.text: Text columns have a toolbox called `.str`. `str.strip()` removes extra spaces at the start and end. `str.lower()` makes everything lowercase, and `str.title()` Makes It Like This. You can chain them: `df["club"].str.strip().str.lower()`.

cells.prompt: Replace ___ with the action that makes everything lowercase, so the club names match. Then press Run to count them again.
Your turn: Maya's name has extra spaces around it. Remove the spaces from the name column for good, then show the name column.

cells.text: Now the fees. They're saved as **text** like "$10", so pandas can't add them up. First, `str.replace("$", "")` swaps every $ for nothing. Then `astype(int)` converts the text into whole numbers (int means integer, a whole number).

cells.prompt: Press Run to make a clean fee_amount column next to the messy one, and compare them.
Your turn: print the total of all the fees, using the clean fee_amount column.
hints: Use sum() on fee_amount, inside print().

cells.text: Dates are often saved as text too. `pd.to_datetime()` turns date text into real dates, so you can find the earliest one, sort them in order or pull out the month later on.

cells.prompt: Last one: convert signup_date to real dates and store it back in the same column. Then print the earliest sign-up date.
hints: Line 1: df["signup_date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["signup_date"]). Line 2: print the min().

recap: The .str toolbox cleans text: strip() removes spaces, and lower() or title() fix capitals. str.replace() plus astype(int) turns "$10" into 10. pd.to_datetime() makes real dates.
